archetype.name: Fringe Contender (run-and-defense)
archetype.definition: A team with a top-six defense and one of the league's best run games whose 5-2 record runs ahead of its middling overall efficiency, because the passing game it keeps leaning on is among the league's worst.

report.headline: Elite run game, top-six defense, and a passing game that keeps stalling
report.take:
Pittsburgh is 5-2 and tied atop the AFC North, but its play looks more like a solid team than a dominant one. Net EPA ranks 16th, right at the league median. The point differential is +15 and implies 3.8 wins, so the record is running about a win and a quarter ahead of the scoreboard (winsOverExpected 1.24, 7th). The franchise has done this every year back to 2020, finishing between 4th and 9th in wins over expected each season. That repeat history makes the close-game edge look more like a trait than a fluke, though it still isn't something to bank on week to week.

The team splits sharply in two. The defense is the foundation: 6th in EPA allowed, 7th against the pass, 8th against the run, 7th on third down, 8th in the red zone, and 5th in points allowed. On offense, the run game is the best thing they do. They rank 2nd in rush EPA and 2nd in yards per carry at 4.84, convert every short-yardage try, and get stuffed rarely. Jaylen Warren has carried most of the load. The passing game is the opposite: 28th in pass EPA, with 22 sacks taken, 30th in the league.

The sacks are the tell. The line allows pressure at only the 12th-highest rate, yet the sack rate is 24th and time to throw is 24th. Aaron Rodgers is holding the ball into sacks more than the protection is collapsing. Despite that, the offense passes more than expected at the 3rd-highest rate in the league, leaning on its weakest unit. The defense has its own hidden cracks. Its pressure rate is 29th, it misses tackles at the 31st-worst rate, and it allows explosive passes at a below-average clip. It wins on structure, tackling short of the sticks in the red zone, and takeaways rather than on pass rush.

The path forward is clear. A team that runs this well and defends this well can win plenty of 20-17 games, and the low penalty count (3rd) and turnover margin help. The ceiling depends on the play-calling trusting the run more, or Rodgers getting the ball out. Until one of those happens, expect a lot of one-score Sundays.

strengths.title: A genuinely elite run game
strengths.body: The ground game ranks 2nd in both rush EPA and yards per carry, and it hasn't failed in short yardage. Yards before contact is only 20th, so the backs are creating a lot of it themselves. The low stuff rate (6th) shows the line is winning at the point of attack often enough. This is the most repeatable thing the offense does, and it carried the 148-yard day in New Orleans.

strengths.title: Top-six defense that wins late downs
strengths.body: The defense ranks 6th in EPA allowed and is balanced, 7th against the pass and 8th against the run. It tightens where it matters: 7th on third down and 8th in red-zone touchdown rate, which is why points allowed (5th) look better than the yardage. Opposing WR1s have been held to the league's lowest EPA per target. History supports it too, with this franchise posting top-eight defensive EPA in several recent seasons.

strengths.title: Clean, low-mistake football
strengths.body: Pittsburgh commits the 3rd-fewest penalties, and its line draws the fewest flags in the league. It also has a +4 turnover margin. That discipline is what turns a median-efficiency team into a close-game winner. It is more sustainable than luck, because it comes from habits rather than bounces.

concerns.title: Passing into the weakest unit
concerns.body: The passing offense is 28th in EPA, yet the team throws more than expected at the 3rd-highest rate. The 22 sacks are mostly a quarterback problem: pressure allowed is only 12th, while sack rate and time to throw are both 24th. This comes down to play-calling and Rodgers' style, so it lasts unless the plan changes.

concerns.title: Record ahead of the efficiency
concerns.body: A 5-2 team with the 16th-ranked net EPA and a differential worth 3.8 wins is living on close games. It is 0.8 in one-score games, and its winsOverExpected ranks 7th. The franchise's history of beating expectation every year softens this, but a few coin flips going the other way would leave a .500-ish team.

concerns.title: No pass rush, shaky tackling
concerns.body: The defense generates pressure at only the 29th-best rate and misses tackles at the 31st-worst rate. That shows up as explosive passes allowed (23rd) and as leaks to secondary targets: WR2, WR3 and TE1 all rank around 19th-21st in EPA allowed. The sack total (9th) is outrunning the pressure, which tends to fade.

trend.note: The defense has been steady every week. The offense has swung from a 3-point day at New England (pass EPA -21.8) to 34 against Indianapolis. Pittsburgh hasn't lost since the short-week defeat in Cleveland, winning the last two on defense and the run game even when the pass game sputtered.

nextGame.headline: Rematch with Cleveland, with the AFC North lead on the line
nextGame.body:
Both teams are 5-2, and Cleveland won the first meeting 27-24 on a Thursday, when Pittsburgh had only four days' rest and Rodgers took five sacks. The Browns are an even bigger record-over-play story: winsOverExpected 2.32 (2nd) against a point differential ranked 22nd. Their offense is 24th in EPA, with a run game ranked 26th and a line that allows sacks at the league's worst rate. Their defense is the real thing, though: 6th against the pass and 6th in sack rate. It also gives up explosive runs more often than any defense in the league, which plays straight into Pittsburgh's strength. The Book has Pittsburgh -3.5 with a 39.5 total. An early forecast shows drizzle and gusts near 22 mph, worth rechecking, and it would only tilt this further toward the ground.

Availability favors Pittsburgh. Cleveland right tackle Tytus Howard (87% of snaps) is questionable after a possible concussion. Guard Teven Jenkins is on IR, which thins an already leaky line. Rotational DT Mike Hall Jr. is out, and CB Myles Harden (63%) is questionable with a hamstring injury. Pittsburgh loses rotational DT Sebastian Joseph-Day (28%) to IR, a small dent in its run-defense depth. WR Ben Skowronek and CB Brandin Echols, both depth pieces, are out.

waysToWin.title: Run straight at the explosive-run leak
waysToWin.body: Cleveland allows explosive runs at the league's worst rate. Pittsburgh is 2nd in rush EPA, and Mike Hall Jr. is out of the Browns' interior. Feeding Warren keeps Rodgers out of obvious passing downs against a good pass rush and shortens a low-total game.

waysToWin.title: Make Watson beat them throwing
waysToWin.body: Cleveland's run game ranks 26th, and Pittsburgh's run defense ranks 8th, so the Browns will be pushed into passing behind the line with the league's worst sack rate. Even Pittsburgh's modest pass rush should find sacks here, especially if Howard sits.

waysToWin.title: Win the hidden yardage
waysToWin.body: Cleveland is 30th in penalties and 31st in line penalties, and its special teams rank 22nd. Pittsburgh is among the cleanest teams in the league. In a game the Book expects to be low-scoring, free yards and drive-killing flags can decide it.

waysToLose.title: A replay of the Week 4 sacks
waysToLose.body: Rodgers took five sacks in Cleveland, and the Browns rank 6th in sack rate. Pittsburgh's own sack rate is 24th, driven by long holds. Stalled drives and a turnover or two would flip a game the defense can otherwise control.

waysToLose.title: Throwing into Cleveland's strength
waysToLose.body: Pittsburgh passes more than expected at the 3rd-highest rate, but Cleveland's pass defense ranks 6th and is 2nd-stingiest against tight ends, so Freiermuth's usual looks are harder to find. If the plan stays pass-first, the offense is playing into the Browns' best unit.

waysToLose.title: Missed tackles turn short throws into chunks
waysToLose.body: Pittsburgh misses tackles at the 31st-worst rate and has been soft against secondary targets and tight ends. Cleveland's offense isn't explosive, but a couple of broken tackles on short throws could hand the Browns the cheap points they otherwise struggle to manufacture.

nextGame.watch: Whether Pittsburgh leans on Warren against the league's most explosive-run-prone defense, or keeps asking Rodgers to hold the ball against a top-six pass rush.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense and the run game are real, and the discipline is a habit rather than a bounce, so this team should keep winning more than it loses. The schedule is mixed. Philadelphia, Houston and Tennessee are soft spots. Denver's 4th-ranked defense, Jacksonville's 5th-ranked offense, Cincinnati on the road and two games with Baltimore are the swing games. The close-game record should cool somewhat, though this franchise has beaten its expected wins every year since 2020, so a full regression to its differential isn't the base case.

The parts most likely to slip are the sack total on defense, which outruns a bottom-four pressure rate, and the offense's tolerance for sacks and drive-killing passes. The part with upside is the play-calling. A team ranked 2nd in rush EPA passing at the 3rd-highest rate over expected is leaving efficiency on the table, and a shift toward the run would steady the offense and protect the defense.
swingFactors: Run-pass balance and Rodgers' time to throw
Whether the defense keeps winning without pressure
Close-game luck in four division games

confidence.note: Seven games is a small sample, but the profile matches the franchise's history.
